problem_type: Director feature flag bootstrap IPC blocks first window
symptom: Flag-off read-only reload walk timed out at Electron launch on the feature branch while origin/main opened normally.
direct_cause: Before first navigation, preload sendSync(feature-proof) was rejected by the normal frame/origin guard; its catch then synchronously sent nomi:log:renderer, whose ipcMain.on guard threw UntrustedIpcSenderError, opening a blocking Electron error dialog and stalling the main process for about 60 seconds.
class_root: Bootstrap diagnostics and feature negotiation were routed through post-navigation IPC assumptions, and the renderer warning path could throw from ipcMain.on instead of returning a contained failure.
migration: Replace the bootstrap IPC handshake with additionalArguments; retain strict assertTrustedSender for every normal channel and defer warnings until the first document is available.
affected_population: Every Electron startup that loads the preload feature proof, especially the flag-off read-only walk and dev harness startup
invariants: The feature flag is still resolved by both processes and fingerprints must match.
Bootstrap IPC accepts only the registered main window webContents.
Post-navigation IPC channels retain the URL and frame trust checks.

door_reduction.why_not: The preload call and main registration are separate sides of the cross-process boundary and both remain explicit.

residual_risks: The fourth-round screenshot set was partly refreshed; the final three-shot light-mode capture remains pending.
internal_only_reason: This is an internal Electron startup ordering and sender-guard invariant.

recurrence.reason: Any future synchronous preload call made before navigation can hit the same URL-dependent guard if it is registered through the normal IPC helper.

generality_proof: Every main window receives the same proof through BrowserWindow webPreferences; preload has no bootstrap IPC dependency, while all post-navigation channels still converge on assertTrustedSender.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Encode the main process feature proof in additionalArguments.
Decode, fingerprint-check, and defer warning emission until navigation.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Feature proof uses the dedicated bootstrap channel and fingerprint mismatch disables the flag.
All other synchronous channels continue to call assertTrustedSender.

prevention.invariant: Pre-navigation feature negotiation must use additionalArguments and must not call IPC.
prevention.failure_mode: Missing or mismatched proof forces the feature off and queues a warning after DOMContentLoaded.
prevention.strategy: Keep bootstrap data one-way from main to preload and reserve IPC for post-navigation channels.

legacy_paths.rationale: No legacy implementation was removed; the existing strict guard remains for normal channels.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No dependency controls this startup ordering invariant.

fix: Pass the main process feature proof through BrowserWindow webPreferences.additionalArguments, parse it in preload without IPC, compare fingerprints locally, and defer mismatch/missing-proof warnings until DOMContentLoaded. Remove the second bootstrap sender guard so all IPC trust decisions remain centralized.
